newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH SPORT7 TV CHANNEL UNDER PRESSURE - MEDIA.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH SPORT7 TV CHANNEL UNDER PRESSURE - MEDIA.

text.p: New Dutch TV channel Sport7 received a double blow at the weekend as ING Barings forecast a large full-year loss for the company and the Dutch soccer association's president criticised its packaging for Amsterdam viewers in a bundle which includes a soft pornography channel.
Sport7 began broadcasting in August and most Dutch vievers can receive it for the standard cable TV fee, but, in and around Amsterdam it forms part of a supplementary pay-TV package.
Het Financieele Dagblad newspaper said on Saturday that investment bank ING Barings estimated that Sport7 would post a loss of 102 million guilders for the 1996/97 financial year.
The paper quoted ING's report as saying that the channel was suffering from poor audience ratings and large start-up costs.
ING said Sport7 needed to link up with other commercial channels to form a powerful pay-TV package, but that it would be two years before sophisticated pay-TV decoders allowed this.
Recent figures from the NOS audience research unit showed that in its first full month of operation, Sport7 gained a four percent share of the Dutch television audience.

In an interview with NRC-Handelsblad newspaper published on Saturday, the president of the Dutch soccer association KNVB, Jos Staatsen, said he was unhappy with the way the Amsterdam cable TV company A2000 had packaged Sport7 with other channels.
"As far as I'm concerned Sport7 should pull out of that package as soon as possible. It's a revolting package. Sport7 is being used to shoe-horn the other channels in," he said.
The KNVB sold exclusive rights for Dutch league soccer to Sport7 in a billion-guilder, seven-year deal and also took a 10 percent stake in the channel.
A2000, which pipes television to households in and around Amsterdam, is a cable TV joint venture between Philips Electronics NV venture and US West .
Its pay-TV package groups Sport7 with a Chinese-language channel CNE and The Adult Channel which features soft-porn.
Sport7 has taken a battering from the Dutch media since its start in August, but Staatsen was unwilling to write the channel off yet.

"Sport7 has not been on the air for two months yet. Some parts of the media have already sounded its death knell. But the public has not yet had the chance to decide. The stakeholders still have complete faith in the venture," he said.
Sport7 is owned by PTT Nederland, ING, Philips Electronics and Dutch TV production firm Endemol (each with 19.5 percent). The KNVB has a 10 percent stake and publisher De Telegraaf five percent.
